newsitem.title: USA: Bank reform to allow direct muni revenue bond sale.
newsitem.headline: Bank reform to allow direct muni revenue bond sale.

text.p: The U.S. House Banking Committee on Wednesday backed a provision in bank reform legislation that would allow U.S. banks to sell municipal revenue bonds directly.
The committee, on a voice vote, rejected an amendment from Rep. Ken Bentsen, a Texas Democrat, that would have eliminated the revenue bond authorization from the bill.
The panel is in its second day of debate over a bill to reform bank laws comprehensively.
If the legislation is enacted, municipal revenue bonds would be considered "bank eligible securities" and banks would not have to establish a separate subsidiary to sell the bonds.
